cv.title: Yordan Hristov — CV
cv.description: CV of Yordan Hristov, Senior Product Designer: AI-ready design systems, design engineering, and seven years of research practice.
cv.ogDescription: Senior Product Designer. AI-ready design systems, design engineering, research practice.

prose.heroLede: I build **AI-ready design systems** with 1:1 code parity and architect the AI workflows that connect product, design, and engineering. Working alongside Technical Product Managers and developers, I help eliminate the traditional handoff by designing systems, optimising processes, and contributing directly to PRDs, prototypes, and production code.
prose.contactKicker: Have a system to build, a surface to audit, or a handoff gap to close?
prose.cvSummary: I build **AI-ready design systems**: component libraries with 1:1 parity between Figma and code, plus custom Claude skills and MCP setups that let agents assemble UI from the real system without drift. I write and ship the frontend myself, reviewed and merged by engineering. Under the tooling sits seven years of research practice — user interviews, usability testing, and WCAG 2.1 AA auditing.

background.prose: Before tech, I spent eleven years helping build and grow a strength and nutrition coaching practice. As the owner's close business partner, I took ownership of many of the systems that defined the business. I led a team of coaches, designed the recruitment and onboarding programme, created the assessment framework used across the practice, conducted hundreds of client interviews, and built a data-driven approach to measuring progress and outcomes.
background.statement: It taught me something design school doesn't: people rarely behave the way they say they will. You have to meet them where they are and design not for what they say, not even what they think they want, but for what they truly need at that moment in their journey.
background.kicker: The research habits started there, not in tech. So did these:

cvOpenSource: Tokens are born in the repo, not in Figma. One `tokens.json` builds the site's CSS variables and a flat JSON that both AI agents and a one-way repo-to-Figma push read — which makes Figma an output of the system rather than its source. Every component ships as a CSS block, a machine-readable spec for agents, and a Storybook story, and **the build fails if any of the three is missing**, so parity is enforced rather than maintained by hand.
Light and dark come from the same token file: a themed colour carries its dark value beside its light one, and the entire theme is {{dark}} re-aliased tokens with zero per-component rules.
prose._cvOpenSourceFactsNote: `0 axe violations across N Storybook stories` is the SCOPED form of the claim. The unscoped `0 accessibility violations` that used to sit here read as a claim about the whole site; the case study has always qualified it correctly as `across the component library — axe-audited per story`, and this line now says the same thing. It is deliberately NOT widened to a screen-reader claim: screen-reader behaviour was not verified in this programme. The story count is `{{components}}` because the design-system build fails a component that has no story, so the two counts are the same number by construction and interpolating it keeps that true.
